about: Generic product types with typical US retail prices that are commonly HSA/FSA eligible and relevant to older adults living at home and their family caregivers, keyed to everyday needs. Eligibility is general guidance from IRS publications and administrator lists, not a guarantee: plans differ, so check with the plan administrator before buying.

eligibility_key.lmn: Usually eligible only with a Letter of Medical Necessity from a clinician
eligibility_key.dual: Dual-purpose: eligible only when bought to treat a medical condition; often needs a letter

needs.label: Trouble walking, standing up, or unsteady on her feet
needs.question: Did the person say they had trouble walking, felt unsteady, struggled to get up from a chair, bed or toilet, or had trouble with stairs?

needs.label: A fall, a near-fall, or fear of falling
needs.question: Did the person say they fell, nearly fell, tripped, slipped, or are afraid of falling?

needs.label: Joint, back or muscle pain
needs.question: Did the person say they had pain or stiffness in their joints, back, hands, knees, hips or muscles?

needs.label: Dizzy or lightheaded
needs.question: Did the person say they felt dizzy, lightheaded, woozy, or that the room was spinning?

needs.label: Nausea or upset stomach
needs.question: Did the person say they felt sick to their stomach, nauseous, queasy, had heartburn or indigestion, or had vomited?

needs.label: Trouble sleeping or up in the night
needs.question: Did the person say they slept badly, could not fall or stay asleep, or were up and about during the night?

needs.label: Forgetting or mixing up medication
needs.question: Did the person say they forgot a pill, were unsure whether they had taken a medicine, took the wrong one, or found their pills confusing?

needs.label: Blood pressure or blood sugar checks
needs.question: Did the person mention their blood pressure, blood sugar, diabetes, or needing to check or record either one?

needs.label: Hard of hearing
needs.question: Did the person say they had trouble hearing people, the TV or the phone, or mention their hearing aids?

needs.label: Trouble seeing or reading
needs.question: Did the person say they had trouble seeing, reading small print, or that their eyes were dry, sore or blurry?

needs.label: Bladder leaks or bathroom urgency
needs.question: Did the person say they had leaks or accidents, had to rush to the bathroom, or got up often at night to use the toilet?

needs.label: Worried about bathing or showering safely
needs.question: Did the person say bathing or showering was hard, tiring or scary, or that they had trouble getting in or out of the tub or shower?

needs.label: Dry or itchy skin, cuts, sores or foot problems
needs.question: Did the person mention dry or itchy skin, a cut, scrape, bruise or sore that is slow to heal, swollen legs or ankles, or problems with their feet?

needs.label: Cold, flu, cough or breathing symptoms
needs.question: Did the person say they had a cold, cough, sore throat, stuffy nose, fever, or felt short of breath?

needs.label: Shaky hands, or trouble eating or swallowing
needs.question: Did the person say their hands shake or tremble, that they had trouble holding a spoon, cup or pen, or that chewing or swallowing was hard or they choked or coughed when eating or drinking?

needs.label: Shaking spells, seizures or blackouts
needs.question: Did the person say they had a seizure, a shaking or jerking spell they could not control, or lost awareness or blacked out?

products.name: Quad-base cane
products.why: A cane with a four-point base that gives more support than a single tip when walking is unsteady.

products.name: Rollator walker with seat
products.why: A four-wheeled walker with hand brakes and a seat for resting on longer walks.
products.note: Listed as 'Walker' on administrator lists.

products.name: Folding walker (two-wheel or standard)
products.why: A lightweight frame to lean on for steady walking indoors.

products.name: Transport or manual wheelchair
products.why: A chair on wheels for trips and longer distances when walking is too tiring.
products.note: IRS Pub 502 lists wheelchairs used for relief of sickness or disability, including upkeep.

products.name: Knee brace or support
products.why: A sleeve or hinged brace that supports a sore or weak knee.

products.name: Back brace or lumbar support belt
products.why: A belt that supports the lower back during daily tasks.
products.note: Supportive cushions and pillows are a different item and usually need a letter.

products.name: Power lift recliner chair
products.why: A recliner that tilts forward to help the person stand up.
products.note: Cigna says a reclining chair is reimbursable only with a medical diagnosis; buyFSA lists recliner chairs as LMN required. Often only the lift mechanism, not the furniture, is reimbursed.

products.name: Stair lift (installed)
products.why: A motorized seat on a rail that carries the person up and down stairs.
products.note: Sources disagree: buyFSA lists stair lifts as eligible; IRS Pub 502 treats lifts as a capital expense that counts only to accommodate a disability (reasonable cost, minus any increase in home value), and administrator lists put home modifications in 'maybe' or LMN. Treat as needing a letter.

products.name: Patient transfer lift
products.why: A hoist that lets a caregiver move the person safely between bed, chair and toilet.
products.note: Listed as eligible by buyFSA. Some plans may still ask for documentation of the disability.

products.name: Reacher / grabber tool
products.why: A long-handled grabber that picks things up without bending or stretching.
products.note: Counts as adaptive equipment. Premera: adaptive equipment qualifies for help with activities of daily living, not for general comfort. Expect to need a letter on card-declined claims.

products.name: Hip protector briefs
products.why: Padded underwear that cushions the hips in a fall.
products.note: Not named on any administrator list checked. Some medical-supply retailers code them as FSA/HSA eligible, but that is not an administrator ruling. Treated cautiously as needing a letter.

products.name: Soft protective headgear
products.why: A padded cap that protects the head in a fall or seizure.
products.note: Not named on administrator lists; falls under adaptive or medical equipment, which plans usually approve with a clinician's letter.

products.name: Personal emergency response (medical alert) system
products.why: A wearable help button, some with fall detection, that calls for help. Price is per month of monitoring, plus any device fee.
products.note: Sources disagree: buyFSA lists medical alert systems as eligible; Cigna says enrollment is reimbursable when accompanied by a medical diagnosis. Treat as needing a letter.

products.name: Medical ID bracelet or necklace
products.why: Jewelry engraved with conditions and medicines, so responders know at a glance.

products.name: Bed assist rail
products.why: A handle that fits under the mattress to help with sitting up and getting out of bed.
products.note: Not named on any administrator list checked; treated as adaptive equipment needing a letter. Bed rails carry entrapment risk, so follow fitting instructions.

products.name: Bed-exit alarm pad
products.why: A pressure pad that sounds a chime for a caregiver when the person gets out of bed.
products.note: Covered only as a medical monitoring device; Workterra's list marks monitoring devices as needing a letter of medical necessity.

products.name: Seizure-alert bed monitor
products.why: A bed sensor that alerts a caregiver to prolonged rhythmic movement at night.
products.note: Medical monitoring device; Workterra's list marks these as needing a letter of medical necessity.

products.name: Bathroom grab bars
products.why: Fixed handholds by the toilet, tub or shower to hold onto when moving.
products.note: IRS Pub 502 lists adding handrails or grab bars anywhere as a medical home modification; installation labor may need separate documentation.

products.name: Clamp-on bathtub safety rail
products.why: A handle that clamps to the tub wall for stepping in and out.
products.note: Premera lists 'Bathtub rails, grips, and safety items' as eligible.

products.name: Shower chair with back
products.why: A waterproof seat so the person can sit, not stand, while showering.
products.note: Commonly misunderstood. Many pharmacies code shower chairs as FSA eligible, but Premera says 'Yes, if required on account of a disability' and Cigna requires a medical diagnosis. Keep a letter on file.

products.name: Tub transfer bench
products.why: A bench that straddles the tub wall so the person can sit and slide in.
products.note: Same treatment as shower chairs: Premera and Cigna tie eligibility to a disability or diagnosis.

products.name: Raised toilet seat
products.why: A seat riser that makes sitting down and standing up from the toilet easier.
products.note: Listed by buyFSA as 'Elevated Toilet Seats: Eligible'.

products.name: Bedside commode
products.why: A portable toilet chair for the bedside when the bathroom is too far at night.

products.name: Toilet bidet attachment
products.why: A spray seat or attachment for cleaning after using the toilet.
products.note: Commonly misunderstood: buyFSA lists bidets as LMN required.

products.name: Adult incontinence briefs or pull-ups
products.why: Absorbent underwear for bladder leaks. Price is per pack.
products.note: Adult incontinence supplies are eligible; baby diapers and diaper services are not.

products.name: Disposable or washable bed underpads
products.why: Absorbent pads that protect the mattress or chair from leaks.
products.note: Covered as incontinence supplies. Ordinary mattress protectors are listed as not eligible.

products.name: Skin barrier or rash cream
products.why: An ointment that protects skin from moisture and irritation.
products.note: Listed as diaper rash ointment/cream. Everyday moisturizers are not eligible.

products.name: Over-the-counter pain reliever
products.why: Standard pain and fever tablets from the pharmacy.
products.note: Over-the-counter medicine is eligible without a prescription since the CARES Act (2020). Some older administrator guides still say 'with prescription'.

products.name: Topical pain relief cream or patch
products.why: A cream, gel or patch applied to sore muscles or joints.
products.note: Over-the-counter medicine is eligible without a prescription since the CARES Act (2020). Some older administrator guides still say 'with prescription'.

products.name: Electric heating pad or wrap
products.why: Steady warmth for stiff or sore muscles and joints.

products.name: Reusable hot/cold gel pack
products.why: A gel pack that can be chilled or warmed for aches and swelling.
products.note: Premera: eligible 'if sold as medical supplies'.

products.name: TENS unit
products.why: A small device that sends mild electrical pulses through skin pads to ease pain.

products.name: Compression arthritis gloves
products.why: Snug gloves that support stiff or achy hands.

products.name: Handheld percussion massager
products.why: A handheld massager for sore muscles.
products.note: Sources disagree: buyFSA lists massage guns as eligible but massage chairs and foot massagers as LMN required; Cigna allows massage chairs only to treat a medical condition. Treat as dual-purpose; keep a letter.

products.name: Over-the-counter motion sickness tablets
products.why: Pharmacy tablets for motion sickness and the queasy, spinning feeling that comes with it.
products.note: Over-the-counter medicine is eligible without a prescription since the CARES Act (2020). Some older administrator guides still say 'with prescription'. Ask a clinician before use, since some cause drowsiness.

products.name: Acupressure wristbands (nausea)
products.why: Wristbands that press on a point on the inner wrist, used for nausea and motion sickness.

products.name: Over-the-counter nausea and upset-stomach remedy
products.why: Pharmacy liquid or chewables for an upset stomach.
products.note: Over-the-counter medicine is eligible without a prescription since the CARES Act (2020). Some older administrator guides still say 'with prescription'.

products.name: Antacid or acid reducer
products.why: Tablets for heartburn and indigestion.
products.note: Over-the-counter medicine is eligible without a prescription since the CARES Act (2020). Some older administrator guides still say 'with prescription'.

products.name: Over-the-counter sleep aid
products.why: A non-prescription medicine for occasional sleeplessness.
products.note: Over-the-counter medicine is eligible without a prescription since the CARES Act (2020). Some older administrator guides still say 'with prescription'. Melatonin is different: it is a supplement and needs a letter.

products.name: Melatonin
products.why: A supplement some people take for sleep.
products.note: Commonly misunderstood: buyFSA lists melatonin as LMN required because it is a supplement, not an OTC drug.

products.name: Light therapy lamp
products.why: A bright lamp used in the morning to help regulate the daily sleep-wake rhythm.
products.note: Sources disagree: buyFSA lists light therapy lamps as eligible; Premera lists seasonal-affective-disorder lights as 'Yes, with prescription'. Treat as needing a letter.

products.name: Alarm pill dispenser
products.why: A locked dispenser that beeps and opens the right compartment at pill time.
products.note: Listed by buyFSA under 'Pill Boxes ... Pill Clocks and Pill Organizers'. Subscription-based connected dispensers may be billed differently.

products.name: Weekly pill organizer
products.why: A box with day-and-time compartments to sort pills a week ahead.
products.note: Cigna lists pill storage containers as eligible.

products.name: Pill cutter or crusher
products.why: A tool for splitting or crushing tablets when they are hard to swallow (check with a pharmacist first).
products.note: Cigna lists pill crushers and cutters as eligible.

products.name: Upper-arm blood pressure monitor
products.why: An automatic cuff for checking blood pressure at home.

products.name: Blood glucose meter
products.why: A small meter for checking blood sugar from a fingertip drop.

products.name: Glucose test strips and lancets
products.why: The single-use strips and lancets a glucose meter needs. Price is per box.

products.name: Fingertip pulse oximeter
products.why: A clip that reads pulse and blood oxygen level.

products.name: Digital thermometer
products.why: A quick read of body temperature.

products.name: Over-the-counter hearing aids
products.why: FDA-regulated hearing aids for adults with perceived mild to moderate hearing loss, bought without an exam.
products.note: IRS Pub 502 includes hearing aids plus batteries, repairs and maintenance. Personal sound amplifiers (PSAPs) are not hearing aids and are deliberately left out of this list.

products.name: Hearing aid batteries
products.why: Replacement batteries for hearing aids. Price is per pack.

products.name: Amplified or captioned telephone
products.why: A phone with extra-loud sound or on-screen captions of what the caller says.
products.note: IRS Pub 502 includes special telephone equipment for people who are hard of hearing. Some plans may ask for documentation; captioned phones may also be free through state or federal programs.

products.name: Earwax removal kit
products.why: Drops and a bulb syringe to soften and rinse out earwax.
products.note: Over-the-counter medicine is eligible without a prescription since the CARES Act (2020). Some older administrator guides still say 'with prescription'.

products.name: Non-prescription reading glasses
products.why: Magnifying glasses for close-up reading.
products.note: Eligible without a prescription per buyFSA and Optum. Non-prescription sunglasses are not.

products.name: Lighted handheld magnifier
products.why: A magnifying glass with a light for small print, labels and pill bottles.

products.name: Lubricating eye drops
products.why: Drops for dry or tired eyes.

products.name: Bandages, gauze and first aid kit
products.why: Dressings and supplies for cuts and scrapes.

products.name: Antibiotic ointment
products.why: An over-the-counter ointment for minor cuts and scrapes.
products.note: Over-the-counter medicine is eligible without a prescription since the CARES Act (2020). Some older administrator guides still say 'with prescription'.

products.name: Medicated itch or eczema cream
products.why: A medicated cream for itchy or irritated skin.
products.note: Commonly misunderstood: medicated creams that treat a skin condition are eligible; everyday lotion and moisturizer are not.

products.name: Graduated compression socks
products.why: Snug socks that squeeze the lower leg, often worn for leg swelling.
products.note: Sources disagree: buyFSA and Cigna list medical compression hosiery as eligible; Optum Financial lists compression hosiery/socks as eligible only with a letter of medical necessity. Athletic compression gear is not eligible.

products.name: Diabetic (non-binding) socks
products.why: Loose-top, seamless socks that avoid pressure and rubbing on sensitive feet.
products.note: Listed as eligible by buyFSA only; not named on the administrator guides checked.

products.name: Cushioned orthotic insoles
products.why: Shoe inserts that cushion and support the arch and heel.
products.note: Sources disagree: buyFSA lists shoe insoles as eligible; Optum Financial lists orthopedic shoes and inserts as dual-purpose needing a prescription or letter; Premera says arch and insole supports need a prescription.

products.name: Cold, flu and cough medicine
products.why: Pharmacy syrups, tablets, lozenges and rubs for cold and flu symptoms.
products.note: Over-the-counter medicine is eligible without a prescription since the CARES Act (2020). Some older administrator guides still say 'with prescription'.

products.name: Cool-mist humidifier
products.why: Adds moisture to dry room air.
products.note: Sources disagree: Cigna lists humidifiers and air purifiers as eligible; Premera says 'Maybe', only if a provider recommends it for a specific condition; buyFSA says LMN required; an Optum Financial list puts humidifiers on its ineligible list. Treat as needing a letter. Air purifiers get the same treatment and are left out here.

products.name: Compressor nebulizer
products.why: A machine that turns liquid medicine into a mist to breathe in.
products.note: The machine is eligible as a medicine delivery device; the inhaled medicines themselves usually need a prescription.

products.name: Tremor-stabilizing spoon
products.why: An electronic handle that offsets hand shaking so food stays on the spoon.
products.note: Not named on administrator lists. As adaptive equipment it qualifies for help with daily living (Premera), and plans usually ask for a clinician's letter.

products.name: Weighted or built-up handle utensils
products.why: Heavier or thicker-handled forks and spoons that are easier to hold steady.
products.note: Adaptive equipment is listed as eligible by buyFSA, but Premera limits it to help with daily living due to disability. Ordinary cutlery is not eligible, so expect to need a letter.

products.name: Weighted wrist cuffs
products.why: Light wrist weights worn to steady the hand for tasks like eating or writing.
products.note: Wrist weights are sold mostly as exercise equipment, which buyFSA lists as LMN required. Treat as dual-purpose.

products.name: Food and drink thickener
products.why: A powder or gel that thickens drinks and soups to a consistency some people find easier to swallow.
products.note: Sources disagree: many medical-supply retailers code thickeners as FSA/HSA eligible, but IRS Pub 502 allows special food only when a physician substantiates the need, and only the cost above a normal diet. Treat as needing a letter.

products.name: Denture adhesive
products.why: Cream or strips that keep dentures in place while eating.
products.note: Listed as eligible by Premera and Optum Financial. Denture cleaning supplies vary by plan.
